title: Of Lawful Oaths and Vows
subtitle: A lawful oath is religious worship, sworn in truth before God; vows are made to God alone, and must be performed with care.

paragraphs.text: A lawful oath is a part of religious worship in which, upon just occasion, the person swearing solemnly calls upon God to witness what he asserts or promises, and to judge him according to the truth or falsity of what he has sworn.

The name of God only is that by which men ought to swear, and it is to be used with all holy fear and reverence. To swear vainly or rashly by that glorious and dreadful name, or to swear at all by any other thing, is sinful and to be utterly avoided. Yet in matters of weight and moment, for the confirmation of truth and the ending of all strife, an oath is warranted by the Word of God under the New Testament as well as the Old, so that a lawful oath, imposed by lawful authority in such matters, ought to be taken.

Whoever takes an oath warranted by the Word of God ought duly to consider the weightiness of so solemn an act, and to assert nothing in it but what he is fully persuaded is the truth. Neither may any man bind himself by oath to anything but what is good and just, what he believes to be such, and what he is able and resolved to perform. Yet it is a sin to refuse an oath touching anything that is good and just, when imposed by lawful authority.

An oath is to be taken in the plain and common sense of the words, without equivocation or mental reservation. It cannot oblige to sin; but in anything not sinful, being taken, it binds to performance, even though it be to a man's own hurt. Nor is it to be violated, even when made to heretics or unbelievers. A vow, which is not to be made to any creature but to God alone, is of the nature of a promissory oath, and ought to be made with the like religious care, and performed with the like faithfulness.
